messages.subject: [statnet_help] Learning ERGM
messages.body_plain:
Dear teachers:
      I have learned statnet package for several month, here I have some questions to ask:
      1.Which term of ERGM should be chosen for interaction of two network covariates ( e.g. an advice network and a support network in a group)? Particularly, I want to know can entrainment effect and exchange effect between two networks be modeled in the same ERGM regression?
      2.An comparison between two variable coefficients can be tested by "Wald test". In the ERGM regression, how to comprare two coefficients ( one for reciprocity, the other for transitivity) by Wald test?
     Thank you for answering my questions in advance.
My best wishes!


Wang (Hopefield) Xi
Sun Yat sen University of China

messages.subject: [statnet_help] AIC and BIC calculations for ergm.ego models
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] AIC and BIC calculations for ergm.ego models
messages.body_plain:
Dear statnet help list,

I am relatively new to ERGMs and I am currently trying to fit a number of ego networks using the ergm.ego package. Some beginner's questions:


1)      Is it possible (or even useful?) to calculate the AIC and BIC of ergm.ego model fits? It seems that the option was included in older versions, but it doesn't seem to work anymore in the newer version (I am using version 0.3.0)?



2)      Options to add complex dependency terms (like gwdegree, gewesp & gwdesp) are not included in the package. Is this something that will be added in the future, or are these not included because these kind of terms are not relevant to model the characteristics of typical ego networks anyway?


Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Kind regards,

Frans Hermans

messages.subject: [statnet_help] GWDSP and ERGM model convergence issue
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] GWDSP and ERGM model convergence issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi statnet,

We?re looking for some guidance on ERGM structural control terms.

Some background: We are analyzing social support networks from two
villages, so are essentially running the same ERGM on two networks. We
decided to add GWDSP to the model after looking at the goodness of fit
plots and seeing room for improvement. For one of the villages, adding
GWDSP to the model (along with mutual and GWESP) improved GOF and model fit
(AIC, BIC, etc). For the second village, adding GWDSP resulted a model that
doesn?t converge.

We?ve tried a number of things to deal with this: increasing the MCMC
sample size and burn-in, adding more iterations (beyond the default 20),
trying other structural control terms (gwodegree, gwidegree), as well as
sweeping through different alpha values for the GW terms (both for all GW
terms and just for the GWDSP term), and we tried removing other covariates
in the model.

None of this has worked. We?d like to have the two ERGMs for the two
villages be easily comparable, ideally by including the same terms in the
two models. Given the model improvement with GWDSP in the first village
(and the fact that the inclusion of GWDSP alters the effect size of some
other covariates), what would you recommend?

1. Does anyone have an idea of how to make GWDSP work in the model that
isn?t converging?

2. Are there other potential structural control terms that we could try?

3. How should we interpret the effect of GWDSP on the first village? The
term is significant, small, and negative. Including it in the model changes
the effect size of some nodeocov terms.

General descriptions of the networks: ~400 nodes, ~3500 edges, directed,
density ~2.3%, reciprocity ~33%

ERGM terms include: age, gender, a kinship network as an edgecov term, a
measure of distance between households as an edgecov term, a few other
basic demographic terms and homophily terms.

We?ve been using both R version 3.2.3 and 3.3.0, and ergm versions 3.5.1
and 3.1.3.

Generally, we are studying the relationship between reputational standing
and social support in these two villages. One of the terms that changes
with the addition of GWDSP is a reputation nodeocov term, one of our terms
of interest, so we?d really like to better understand what is behind this.

Any help would be much, much appreciated!

- Elly Power and Elspeth Ready

-- 
Eleanor A. Power
Omidyar Fellow
Santa Fe Institute
1399 Hyde Park Rd, Santa Fe, NM 87501
www.santafe.edu/~epower
